48ddbe1946 ""cgroup: make css->refcnt clearing on cgroup removal
optional"" allowed a css to linger after the associated cgroup is
removed.  As a css holds a reference on the cgroup's dentry
that cgroup dentries may linger for a while.
Destroying a superblock which has dentries with positive refcnts is a
critical bug and triggers BUG() in vfs code.  As each cgroup dentry
holds an s_active reference
column2: any lingering cgroup has both its dentry

column1: and the superblock pinned and thus preventing premature release of
superblock.
Unfortunately
releasing a cgroup which is directly under the root of the hierarchy.
When a cgroup directory is released
corresponding dentry and then invokes dput() on the parent
recurse further
column2: so when a cgroup directly below root cgroup is

column1: released
column2: the cgroup is first destroyed - which releases the s_active

column1: it was holding - and then the dentry for the root cgroup is dput().
This creates a window where the root dentry's refcnt isn't zero but
superblock's s_active is.  If umount happens before or during this
window
column2: vfs will see the root dentry with non-zero refcnt and trigger

column1: BUG().
Before 48ddbe1946
column2: this problem didn't exist because the last dentry

column1: reference was guaranteed to be put synchronously from rmdir(2)
invocation which holds s_active around the whole process.
Fix it by holding an extra superblock->s_active reference across
dput() from css release
column2: which is the dput() path added by 48ddbe1946

column1: and the only one which doesn't hold an extra s_active ref across the
final cgroup dput().
